summary: Covington County, Alabama Forest Service tower built by CCC Company 3474 in 1938-39 with a wooden cab; unstaffed since about 1975; rehabilitated 2006.

facts.design: 100-foot structure made by Jones & Laughlin Steel, with 12 by 12 foot wooden cab and catwalk

access.note: The Forest Service lists the Open Pond Recreation Area as open; Wikipedia says it is set aside for hiking, fishing, bicycling and camping; the sources do not say whether visitors may go up the tower

events.note: Built 1938-39 by Company 3474 of the CCC (Register); a plaque at the tower gives 1938 (Wikipedia)
Unstaffed since about 1975 (Register); blog says not staffed since 1975
Registered December 30, 1994 as US 97, AL 1; nominated by John Yancy, Forest Supervisor
Rehabilitated fall and winter 2006: roof, steps, catwalk, replica windows and door, repaint; fire finder cleaned by March 2007
Visit report October 23, 2007: recent roof and repaint, looks good
Visit report January 6, 2009: state antennae noted as an encroachment
Visit report July 24, 2015: good condition; NHLR sign missing; no signed directions to tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 1938-39 for construction; the plaque reading reported by Wikipedia gives 1938. Both agree construction began in 1938, so the event is recorded as 1938.
The Register dates the rehabilitation to fall and winter 2006; the blog says approximately 2007. The story uses the Register's 2006 date and reports the blog's version.

notes_for_editor: Register entry has the most detail and three dated visit reports (2007, 2009, 2015); the latest visit is from 2015, so current condition is not confirmed. The plaque date comes via Wikipedia; no photo of the plaque was read. Tower interior access is not described in any source. The Register's visit-report 'Staffed? No' is the basis for the staffing as_of date.
